Q: Does SQL window function ORDER BY inherit from parent query ORDER BY? A:

The fiddle results are not the same, so the clear answer is No it doesn't. If you get similar results it's only due to luck.

In the first case, the order of rows itself isn't guaranteed. Without an ORDER BY clause there's no implied order, not even a storage order. The database is free to return the data in any order, and not ordering is the cheapest option.

Using different ordering in the query and window function can have performance implications too. If the same ordering is used, the database can sort the data once before calculating the window functions :

SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY group_id ORDER BY timestamp DESC) as rn
FROM events
ORDER BY timestamp DESC;

If the ORDER clauses contradict each other, the database will have to sort twice. Once to calculate the window function and once again to sort the query results

SELECT *, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY group_id ORDER BY timestamp DESC) as rn
FROM events
ORDER BY timestamp;

Q: Distribution center Anylogic A:

It is really hard to know how you are modeling what you are modeling.

First of all: do you have a clear rule for what are the docks? If they are resources, you can probably just use normal Seize/Release blocks, or Service blocks and the truck will go to any free dock. If not, can you think of the rules you need? Are they able to be represented solely by SelectOutput blocks? If so, you can probably make a chain of SelectOutput to make the truck go to the desired dock.

Although, in general, I would strongly recommend you learn basic Java for AnyLogic. I can't see you making any relevant model (even for learning) from input reading to having some outputs with zero java knowledge. Even the SelectOutput blocks might need a little bit of java, and you might need some basic java to measure times, queues, generate some statistics.

Q: Prevent depth warning in Powershell ConvertTo-Json when explicitly specifing the Depth? A:

This seems to be a bug/regression in pwsh - it works as expected in WindowsPowerShell (5.x)

in pwsh, you could set $WarningPreference to get rid of the message like so:

$WarningPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'  
$x | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 1

or alternatively

$x | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 1 -WarningAction:SilentlyContinue

as C3roe / Martin Ba suggested in the comments
